\[
\lambda' = \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\mu \in \{\lambda_1 + \alpha\lambda_2,\ \lambda_2 + \alpha\lambda_1\}} \lvert\mu\rvert,
\qquad
N_\sigma = \frac{\max(\lambda', 0)}{\max_x \max(\lambda', 0)},
\qquad
\alpha = \tfrac{1}{3}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda_1, \lambda_2\): The Hessian eigenvalues
- \(\alpha\): The mixing constant, 1/3
- \(N_\sigma\): The neuriteness at scale sigma, from 0 to 1

The Hessian is the matrix of second derivatives of the image smoothed by a Gaussian of sigma. Meijering's measure mixes each eigenvalue with a third of the other and keeps the one of the larger size. This changes the shape of the response across a line, so long, flat lines stand out. Negative values are set to 0, and each scale is divided by its largest value over the image, so every scale reaches 1. The filter keeps the largest value over the scales and stretches the result so the strongest response is white. scikit-image uses alpha = 1/3 by default.
